title: Beyond Advertising: Mechanism Design for Platform-Wide Marketing Service “QuanZhanTui”

problem.claim: The paper studies mechanism design for a platform-wide marketing service that must balance sellers' welfare with the platform's user experience.

gap.claim: Conventional ad bidding focuses on impressions from ad traffic even though most sellers' sales come from organic traffic, leaving the relationship between ad spending and total sales uncertain and creating operational inefficiency.

contributions.claim: The stock-constrained value maximizer model represents sellers' joint requirements for marketing efficiency and platform-wide return on investment.
The Liquid Payment Auction is proposed to optimize the balanced objectives while accounting for sellers' requirements in an auto-bidding environment.
Under mild assumptions, the paper proves optimality and incentive compatibility properties for the Liquid Payment Auction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the Liquid Payment Auction outperforms conventional auctions in extensive experiments on QuanZhanTui.
The authors report that the payment rule based on sellers' liquid welfare provides a clearer link between investment and total sales.
The authors report desirable theoretical properties for the Liquid Payment Auction under mild assumptions.

narrative_sequence.summary: E-commerce sellers bid for ad impressions, while most sales arise from organic traffic.
The uncertain relationship between ad spending and total sales creates operational inefficiency.
QuanZhanTui extends bidding to the platform's entire traffic to increase total sales without compromising user experience.
The paper formulates a multi-objective mechanism design problem, introduces a stock-constrained value maximizer model, and proposes the Liquid Payment Auction.
The authors report theoretical properties and superior experimental performance compared with conventional auctions.

source_observation.claim: When a seller's sales depend substantially on organic traffic, optimizing only paid impressions can leave the relationship between spending and total sales uncertain.

interpretation.claim: Marketing mechanisms may need objectives and feedback signals tied to platform-wide outcomes rather than only directly purchased impressions.

application.claim: For platform-wide marketing allocation, evaluate mechanisms using both seller welfare and platform-level experience or return objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach applies beyond the QuanZhanTui setting or under conditions different from the stated assumptions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact mild assumptions used for the theoretical results.
The abstract does not provide experimental datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the operational implementation or deployment scope of QuanZhanTui.
